- [Your Camera's Sensor Is Colorblind. Here Is How It Fakes Color](https://camerasdecoded.com/blog/bayer-filter-colorblind-sensor.html)
  Fstoppers explains that every photosite on your sensor is a grayscale light meter, and color arrives through a 1975 Kodak patent: the Bayer mosaic, half green to match human vision. Demosaicing then rebuilds two-thirds of every pixel, which is why raw files look different in every converter.
  In short: Every photosite on a digital sensor only counts light, not color, so your camera is technically colorblind. A Bayer filter array, a mosaic of red, green, and blue filters patented by Kodak's Bryce Bay

## About

Cameras Decoded is a Duolingo-style photography education platform. The blog covers camera gear, shooting technique, and industry news for mirrorless photographers.

- Main site: https://camerasdecoded.com
- Blog index: https://camerasdecoded.com/blog-updates.html
